Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest

Class BehaviorSchedulerGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.BehaviorSchedulerGameTestsLogic
public final class BehaviorSchedulerGameTestsLogic extends Object
Server-side coverage for ServerBehaviorScheduler â€” the authority for which behavior a mob is playing and when. BehaviorDeterminismGameTestsLogic covers the client's animation derivation; this drives the server clock by hand (serverTick()) and probes the schedule through trigger()'s return (a dropped trigger means the mob is busy or asleep). Every test forces the scheduler to a clean slate with clear() and force-and-restores the behavior config it touches; ambient play is disabled so only the events under test can move the schedule, except where ambient rolls are what's under test. The sleeping villager's lids, which the client derives from vanilla's synced sleep state, is covered here too, since sleep is the one state that blocks the schedule, and so is the swelling creeper's rattle, derived the same way from vanilla's synced swell, the ramming goat's squint, the aiming archer's and player's one-eyed squint, the angry red pupils, and the creepy enderman's pulse, each also with its server switch off. The mid-effect start-tracking catch-up packet and the anger packet need a connected client and stay source-verified.

  • Method Details

    • affectionEventsPlayLove

      public static void affectionEventsPlayLove(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      The vanilla affection events play love, through the server's entity-event broadcast, and only while loveOnAffection is on; other entity events play nothing. In game: feed wheat to an eyed cow, watch an eyed iron golem offer a villager a flower, breed eyed villagers, or tame an eyed ocelot with raw fish, and the mob's pupils swell to fill its eyes and shrink back. With loveOnAffection = false none of them change the eyes.

    • aimingArcherWinks

      public static void aimingArcherWinks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A skeleton drawing its bow squints the eye on its off-hand side and keeps the other open, still plays behaviors while it does, and opens the eye again once it lets go; a left-handed skeleton squints the other eye. Other archers don't: a pillager charging its crossbow keeps both eyes open. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against server mobs whose item use is set by hand, since the squint is derived from the item use vanilla syncs rather than sent. In game: in survival, approach an eyed skeleton; one eye narrows each time it draws its bow and opens when it fires.

    • aimingPlayerWinks

      public static void aimingPlayerWinks(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A player drawing a bow closes the eye opposite the arm holding it for as long as the draw is held, and opens it again on release: the left eye for a bow in a right-handed player's main hand, the right eye for a bow in the off hand or a left-handed player's main hand. Charging a crossbow keeps both eyes open. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against mock players whose item use is set by hand. In game: apply a Slimy Eye to yourself, switch to third person, and draw and hold a bow; the eye on the side away from the bow narrows until you loose the arrow.

    • angerFollowsEntityLifetime

      public static void angerFollowsEntityLifetime(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Server-reported anger survives renderer resets but ends with the entity or client level. In game: provoke an eyed golem, leave tracking distance, let it calm, and return; its pupils are calm. Repeat while another player stays near it, then change dimensions. Resource reload while the angry golem remains loaded must keep its red pupils. This test drives the runtime operations; real packet lookup and loader unload delivery require the connected-client reproduction.

    • angryMobsHaveRedPupils

      public static void angryMobsHaveRedPupils(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      An attacking mob's pupils ease to red, stay red under a behavior, and ease back when it stops; the server's anger report does the same, and a tracker built for a mob already reported angry starts red. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against a server zombie. In game: let an eyed zombie chase you and its pupils turn red; outrun it until it gives up and they fade back.

    • healSwirlIsRateLimited

      public static void healSwirlIsRateLimited(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      A heal swirl is rate-limited per mob: a second heal inside the cooldown is dropped even while the mob is idle.     • oneBehaviorAtATimeUntilItElapses

      public static void oneBehaviorAtATimeUntilItElapses(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      "One at a time, non-interruptable": a trigger is dropped while another behavior plays, allowed once it elapses. In game: as a creative operator, look at an eyed mob and run /sg admin behavior swirl, then /sg admin behavior blink while it swirls; the blink does not play. Run it again after the swirl ends and it does.

    • rammingGoatSquints

      public static void rammingGoatSquints(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A goat lowering its head to ram squints, still plays behaviors while it does, and opens its eyes again once the ram ends and its head comes back up. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against a server goat given the ram entity events by hand, since the squint is derived from the head position vanilla sets from them rather than sent. In game: stand in front of an eyed goat until it lowers its head and charges; its eyes narrow for the charge and open again afterwards.

    • sleepingMobPlaysNoBehaviors

      public static void sleepingMobPlaysNoBehaviors(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player)
      A sleeping mob plays nothing: the admin trigger, heal, trade, affection, and ambient rolls are all dropped until it wakes. In game: as an operator at night, look at a sleeping eyed villager and run /sg admin behavior swirl; it reports the behavior dropped. Hit the villager to wake it and run the command again, and it plays.

    • sleepingVillagerClosesLids

      public static void sleepingVillagerClosesLids(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A sleeping villager's eyelids close to a slit over its full-size eyes, stay closed until it wakes, and open back out of sight; a tracker built for an already-sleeping villager starts with them closed, and no behavior starts on the client while it sleeps. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against a server villager, since the lids are derived from vanilla's synced sleep state rather than sent. In game: at night, watch an eyed villager go to bed; tan lids slide in over each eye from above and below, leaving a slit across the middle, stay that way until it wakes, then slide back out and vanish.

    • swellingCreeperRattles

      public static void swellingCreeperRattles(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A swelling creeper's pupils keep rattling around its eyes, and settle again once it shrinks back; at rest they hang still. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly against a server creeper ticked by hand, since the agitation is derived from vanilla's synced swell rather than sent; the swell is reversed well before the fuse runs out. In game: walk up to an eyed creeper until it hisses, then back away; its pupils fly around frantically while it swells and drop back to rest after it shrinks.

    • switchedOffOngoingBehaviorsStayNeutral

      public static void switchedOffOngoingBehaviorsStayNeutral(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Each ongoing behavior stays neutral while its server switch is off, and a sleeping mob still plays no expression with its squint off. Drives the client-side GooglyTracker directly with settings that switch one behavior off at a time, against the same vanilla states the "on" tests use. In game, with each key set to false in somegoogly-server.toml: with squintOnSleep, a sleeping eyed villager shows no lids and a sleeping player with a Slimy Eye keeps their eyes open; with squintOnRam, a charging eyed goat keeps its eyes open; with winkOnAim, an eyed skeleton drawing its bow keeps both eyes open; with rattleOnSwell, a hissing eyed creeper's pupils hang still; with pulseWhenCreepy, a screaming eyed enderman's pupils hold their size; with angryEyes, an eyed zombie chasing you keeps its pupil color.
